style: Thoughtful, warm, clear and unhurried. Grade 9 algebra studio.
lines: Press x squared, x or 1 to drop a tile, or drag one onto the mat. A red tile on a matching solid tile makes zero.
Pick a card from the list. Then drag its tiles into the frame until they close into a rectangle.
Pick a card from the expression list to start a square.
Press a tile button to add a tile. Select a tile to use its enabled tray controls, or move it with the arrow keys.
Drag a pile tile into the frame, or select a tile and tap a dashed cell.
Press Split strips to share the x strips evenly between two edges.
Press Fill the corner. Every unit added inside gets a negative unit outside, so the expression stays the same.
Drag the number-line dot, or use its arrow keys. Find where the inset square vanishes.
Press Start over to restore this expression and rebuild its square.
Stuck? Press Zero pair. It changes the picture, not the value.
Not closed yet. Read the tip, move a tile, then press Check.
It closes. The edges are the factors.
Right. No whole-number rectangle exists for this one.
This one does close. Read the tip and keep building.
The square is done. What is left over is the smallest value.
A positive tile and its matching negative make zero. The expression stays the same.
Added zero.
Choose a tile from the tile list. Use the arrow buttons to place and move it. The enabled tray buttons edit that tile.
Read the factors and zeros. Choose another expression card, or press Start over to build this one again.
Compare every factor-pair sum in the tip with the middle coefficient. Then choose another expression card.
